title: What Is a Stop-Loss? The Safety Net Beginners Should Know
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. A stop-loss is an order that closes a position at a set price to limit a loss. Sources: Investopedia, Fidelity. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: PRICE DROPS FAST. NOW WHAT?
scenes.narration: Crypto prices can fall fast. Many traders use a tool to limit the damage. It is called a stop-loss.

scenes.head: WHAT IS A STOP-LOSS?
items: Triggers at a price you pick
scenes.narration: A stop-loss is an order you set in advance. When the price reaches your chosen level, it sells automatically to limit a loss.

scenes.head: A SIMPLE EXAMPLE
scenes.narration: Say a coin costs one hundred dollars and your stop is ninety. If the price falls to ninety, the order is triggered.

scenes.head: WHY PEOPLE USE IT
scenes.narration: Traders use it to take emotion out of decisions, set a limit up front, and avoid watching the screen all day.

scenes.head: IT IS NOT PERFECT
scenes.sub: FAST MARKETS CAN SLIP PAST IT
scenes.narration: It is not a guarantee. In a fast market the price can jump past your level, so you may sell lower than planned.

scenes.head: BEFORE YOU USE ONE
scenes.narration: Learn how your platform handles stop orders, know the fees, and never risk money you cannot afford to lose.
